q: A function f ∈ BV([a,b]) (bounded variation) can be decomposed (Lebesgue decomposition) into:
opts: Absolutely continuous and Cantor parts only
Absolutely continuous part f_{ac}, jump part f_j (step function), and Cantor part f_c (continuous, but derivative = 0 a.e.)
exp: Lebesgue decomposition of BV functions: f = f_{ac} + f_j + f_c (three parts). The Cantor part is the subtle component: it is continuous, singular (derivative 0 a.e.), and carries mass on a set of measure zero (like the Cantor function). All three parts are BV.
